construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(T)=T^{16}+T^9+T^4+T^2+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p),
\]
and write \(\alpha=T\bmod p\). Every \(z\in F\) has unique coordinates \(z=\sum_{i=0}^{15}z_i\alpha^i\).

Fix the evaluation set
\[
A=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}u_i\alpha^i:u_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\qquad |A|=2^{15},
\]
ordered by \(\sum_i u_i2^i\). For \(z\in F\), define its affine Boolean block
\[
\Phi(z)=\left(z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_iv_i\right)_{v\in\mathbb F_2^{15}},
\]
with \(v\) in binary-integer order.

For every
\[
f(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{64}c_jX^j\in F[X],
\]
define
\[
C(f)=\bigl(\Phi(f(a))_v\bigr)_{(a,v)\in A\times\mathbb F_2^{15}},
\]
ordered first by \(a\), then by \(v\). Set \(C=\{C(f):\deg f\le64\}\). No sampling, shortening, puncturing, repetition, or padding occurs.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: A compact deterministic model of \(\mathbb F_{2^{16}}\) is \(\mathbb F_2[T]/(T^{16}+T^9+T^4+T^2+1)\). Repeated squaring gives \(r_8=T^{15}+T^{10}+T^3\) and \(r_{16}=T\). With \(h=r_8+T\), \((T^{11}+T^{10}+T^6+T^5+1)p+(T^{12}+T^{11}+T^5+T^4+T)h=1\), providing a one-line Rabin certificate.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Can one construct deterministically either a binary \([16384,16,8185]\) code or a binary \([8192,17,4090]\) code? Concatenation with, respectively, \([65536,66,65471]_{2^{16}}\) or \([131072,62,131011]_{2^{17}}\) Reed–Solomon gives dimensions 1056 or 1054 and distances 535,880,135 or 535,834,990. Their Griesmer sums are only 16,374 and 8,185, so Griesmer does not close these concrete gateways.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

The displayed construction is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[1{,}073{,}741{,}824,1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2.
\]
Its campaign status should remain under review until the repository verification workflow is recorded.

## Field certificate

Let \(r_0=T\) and \(r_{i+1}=r_i^2\bmod p\). Direct reduction gives
\[
r_8=T^{15}+T^{10}+T^3,\qquad r_{16}=T.
\]
Put \(h=r_8+T=T^{15}+T^{10}+T^3+T\). Direct multiplication in \(\mathbb F_2[T]\) gives
\[
(T^{11}+T^{10}+T^6+T^5+1)p
 +(T^{12}+T^{11}+T^5+T^4+T)h=1.
\]
Thus \(p\mid T^{2^{16}}+T\) and \(\gcd(p,T^{2^8}+T)=1\). Since 2 is the only prime divisor of 16, Rabin's criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Hence \(F\) is the explicitly represented field of order \(2^{16}\).

## Inner and outer maps

The map \(\Phi\) is binary linear and injective: its value at \(v=0\) recovers \(z_0\), and comparison with its values at the fifteen unit vectors recovers \(z_1,\ldots,z_{15}\). If the linear part is nonzero, the affine function is balanced and has weight \(2^{14}\). If the linear part vanishes and \(z\ne0\), then \(z=1\), producing the all-one block of weight \(2^{15}\).

The outer message space has dimension 65 over \(F\). Evaluation on \(A\) is injective because a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 64 cannot vanish at all 32,768 distinct points. It also has at most 64 evaluation roots, so every nonzero outer word has at least 32,704 nonzero symbols.

Both maps are binary linear and injective. Therefore
\[
\dim_{mathbb F_2}C=16\cdot65=1040,
\qquad
|A|\,2^{15}=2^{30}.
\]

## Minimum distance

Every nonzero polynomial produces at least 32,704 nonzero blocks, each of weight at least \(2^{14}\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(f))\ge32704\cdot2^{14}
=(2^{15}-2^6)2^{14}
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.
\]
This covers every nonzero codeword.

For attainment, let \(R\) be the first 64 elements of \(A\) and set
\[
g(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r).
\]
The set \(g(A\setminus R)\subset F^*\) has at most 32,704 elements, whereas \(|F^*|=65,535\). Let \(z\) be the first nonzero field element outside this image and put \(f=z^{-1}g\). Then \(f\) vanishes exactly on \(R\) and never equals 1 elsewhere. Every remaining symbol therefore has a nonzero linear part under \(\Phi\), so all 32,704 remaining blocks have weight exactly \(2^{14}\). This proves
\[
d_{\min}(C)=535{,}822{,}336.
\]

## Scoped ceiling

If a 32,768-coordinate binary inner code has distance at least 16,384 and dimension 17, its Griesmer sum is 32,769, which is impossible. Thus its dimension is at most 16. A product-distance certificate needs outer block distance at least 32,704; puncturing 32,703 coordinates is injective, so Singleton bounds the outer cardinality by \((2^{16})^{65}\). Consequently this equal-block product architecture cannot exceed 1040 binary dimensions, and the construction attains that ceiling.
